chapters.name: Cold open
lines: For as long as there has been money, a person has stood behind every payment.
A signature. A card. A click.
That is changing.
Software is learning to act on our behalf. To search. To negotiate. To buy.
And soon, to spend.

chapters.name: Brand reveal
lines: Abstraxn.
Superpowering the agent economy.

chapters.name: The shift
lines: AI agents are no longer demos.
They book travel, call APIs, pay for data and settle invoices. At machine speed, around the clock.
Every one of those actions needs a way to hold money, and a way to spend it.
But the financial system was built for people. Not for software that makes decisions.

chapters.name: The problem
lines: Today, we know how to answer three questions.
Know Your Customer tells you who a person is.
Know Your Transaction tells you where money moved.
Know Your Agent tells you which software is acting.
Each one tells you who. None of them tells you what was authorised.
And none carries a rule an agent can actually be stopped by.
So most teams discover what their agent spent in a log they read afterwards.

chapters.name: Know Your Intent
lines: Abstraxn introduces a fourth layer. Know Your Intent.
It begins with a Precept. Signed spend authority, bound to an agent's identity. A cap. A period. An allowlist. An expiry.
Then, before any money moves, every payment is checked against it.
Allowed. Denied. Or routed to a human. In under fifty milliseconds.
And every decision, including every refusal, produces a signed receipt that anyone can verify.
Identity tells you who. Intent tells you what they authorised.

chapters.name: Settlement layer
lines: Beneath the Authority Gate sits a complete settlement layer.
Embedded wallets give every user, and every agent, an ERC-4337 smart account. Secured by passkeys and social recovery. No seed phrases.
The Bundler packages operations, and simulates them before they ever reach the chain.
The Paymaster sponsors gas, with per-agent budgets and daily caps, payable in USDC or other tokens.
And the Relayer makes sure every transaction lands. Managing nonces, bumping gas, and resubmitting anything that gets stuck.
Ethereum. Base. Arbitrum. Polygon.

chapters.name: One payment, end to end
lines: Here is what that looks like, end to end.
A travel agent is given a Precept. Five hundred dollars a month. Airlines only. Valid until December.
It finds a fare for six hundred and twenty dollars. The check runs. Denied. Over the cap. A human is asked to approve.
It finds another fare. Three hundred and eighty dollars. Allowed.
The Paymaster covers the gas. The Relayer lands the transaction.
And a signed receipt is written. For the payment, and for the refusal before it.

chapters.name: The agent economy
lines: With authority and settlement in place, something new becomes possible.
Not a store. An economy.
Agents discover services, and pay for them on-chain, through x402.
More than fifty services are already integrated. From data and browsing, to email and phone.
And businesses can list what they sell, directly to agents.

chapters.name: Proof
lines: The infrastructure is already proven.
More than five billion dollars in routed volume.
Ninety-nine point nine percent submission success, across more than a hundred thousand transactions.
And recognised among TOKEN2049's NEXUS Top 50.

chapters.name: Close
lines: The agent economy needs rules it can be held to.
Set what an agent may spend. Prove who it is. Check both before it pays. And keep a receipt anyone can verify.
So. What does your agent do on day one?
Abstraxn. Superpowering the agent economy.
